correctness.rationale: For fixed skew A with 0<a_ij<1 above diagonal and iid fair signs, each coordinate X_{n,i} is a bounded martingale. Its exact conditional square increment is Xi²(A X)_i², so the sum of expected increments is finite and the almost sure limit Y obeys Yi(A Y)_i=0. In any support with ≥2 positive coordinates, its smallest index has strictly positive row interaction, contradiction; therefore Y is a simplex vertex. Martingale expectations give P(I=i)=x_i, even from boundary starts. For initially all-positive x, factors remain in [1−ρ,1+ρ]; log increments converge in Cesàro to iid log(1+σ a_{ji}) at a realized vertex, and a common SLLN event gives loser exponent 1/2 log(1−a_{jI}²). The use of signs from the original iid sequence is legitimate even conditioned on I since the SLLN is an unconditional probability-one event. Exact rational one-step checks and small sign-word enumeration corroborate but do not prove the infinite result.

Exact initial-weight fixation and pairwise extinction exponents are a distinct natural transitive subfamily.

value.rationale: The exact fixation law equal to starting fractions and pathwise pairwise loss exponents under a natural unbiased environmental switch yield an interpretable general-dimensional theorem. It separates stochastic coexistence uncertainty from deterministic transitive advantage, going beyond routine martingale convergence by proving vertex support collapse.

limitations: Skew transitive 0<a_ij<1 above diagonal, iid unbiased switching, finite m≥2; decay rate only for initially strictly positive data. No finite-horizon mixing or fluctuations.
